panels.description: Wide, full page width. A road clinging to the edge of the land. On the left, palm groves and pepper gardens climb gentle slopes; on the right, low cliffs drop to a strip of sand and a flat grey ocean. Two small riders seen from behind, heading south in a salt haze.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They did not take me to a palace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The bulls were gone. This time I rode, though not as I had once ridden.

panels.description: Medium, the two riders side by side, riding toward us. Nagoji on a small, rough-coated coastal horse with a suspicious eye, smaller than any Deccan mare. Nagoji is bare-headed and unarmed: simple cream shirt, cotton dhoti, long curly hair tied back, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no sword, no sash, no turban. His bandaged hands are light on the reins and his spine is straight. Ibrahim on a sturdy pony on the near side, his LEFT cheek turned to us so the scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw reads: shorter than the fishermen but broader, white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets over a pale vest and white mundu. He pats one pocket. He has caught Nagoji looking.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Gifts. Information costs, *bhau*. So do favours.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: When we reach the hall, remember that.

panels.description: The largest panel on the page. The road dips to a narrow inlet, dark and still. Boats drawn up along its banks, broad-bellied cargo craft and slender river canoes, cooking smoke drifting. On the rise beyond, an outer wall of rough red stone blocks topped with a musketeers' parapet; inside it a long hall on wooden pillars carved with vines and tigers, its long side open toward the sea. Behind, on higher ground, a rampart runs inland along the shape of the land. Not large. Purpose in every line.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (small, soft)
copy.text: This is only one claw. The kingdom itself is the beast.

panels.description: The gate. Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes, matchlocks and spears, alert but not nervous. One raises a hand in greeting to Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets, scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw). Nagoji in the foreground, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt, turning his head sharply at the words.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: The king is in council. You are expected.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In most kingdoms I had known, a stranger waited days for an audience. Here the king himself waited at the end of the road.

panels.description: Narrow strip, bottom. Nagoji dismounted, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt, his bandaged hand on the coastal horse's neck. The horse has tossed its head away from him, toward the groom taking its reins. Nagoji is still patting a neck that is already leaving.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kanka would have nudged my shoulder.

panels.description: From the top of a short flight of stone steps, behind Nagoji and Ibrahim (white turban, dark short coat) as they step out of the glare into a cooler hall. High roof, dark rafters, mats on the floor. Men sit cross-legged in loose rows, leaving a clear lane down the centre to a raised platform at the far end. The long side of the hall on screen LEFT stands open between pillars, and through it, below, the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the Deccan, kings received men in high halls thick with incense, with carpets to muffle footsteps and paintings to remind visitors who held power.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here, when the hall fell quiet, you could still hear the sea.

panels.description: Large. Down the clear lane to the far end: a slightly raised wooden platform, and on it MARTHANDA VARMA (attach `concepts/varma-v1.png` and use the sheet for his FACE ONLY). Tall, bare-chested, a single cream-and-gold cloth thrown over one shoulder, gold necklaces, simple Vaishnavite lines on his forehead. A cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest, no crown. A spear rests against his shoulder. A rolled map lies open on the mat before him; a sword lies within easy reach, its hilt worn smooth by use rather than polished for show. He is looking at the map, not toward the camera. At his left hand (screen right), small and in shadow, Ramayyan sits at a low table in plain white cloth. The open side of the hall runs down screen left, and sea light falls across the platform from that side.

Close. Ibrahim at Nagoji's ear, lips barely moving, hand resting on a clinking pocket (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat, scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw). Nagoji in profile, listening: bare-headed, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. Beyond them, small and soft at the far end of the lane, Marthanda Varma on his platform, in his cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest. The open side of the hall on screen left.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Marthanda Varma. And his diwan.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Remember what I said about gifts.

panels.description: Medium, beside the platform: RAMAYYAN. Thin frame, sharp fine features, receding hair; his upper body wrapped in plain white cloth (not bare-chested), no jewellery, no crest, no spear. A low table before him with palm-leaf bundles, an ink pot and a stylus. His eyes are on the newcomers, and on everything else. The king is out of frame. In the near foreground, two seated men lean their heads together, whispering. Sea light from the open side falls from screen left.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ramayyan. He spoke Persian and Dutch and every trade tongue of this coast.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the entrance end, low behind the shoulders of the seated rows: Nagoji walking into the clear space, small against the length of the hall, heads along both rows turning to follow him. Ibrahim (white turban, dark short coat) a step behind him at the start of the lane. Marthanda Varma small on his platform at the far end, in his cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest. The open side of the hall on screen left.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The back of my neck prickled, as it always did when I walked alone into a space where everyone else already knew their place.

panels.description: From the entrance end, the open side of the hall on screen left. Nagoji bowing, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands: not as deeply as a subject would, but enough to set the man on the platform apart from a fellow soldier. Ibrahim a pace behind him and to one side, toward the open side (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat), smooth, one open hand gesturing forward toward Nagoji. Marthanda Varma small on his platform at the far end, eyes still on his map (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest), Ramayyan in white cloth at his left hand (screen right).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Your Majesty. This is the Maratha rider I wrote of.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: He comes from Portuguese chains and storm water, and he carries knowledge of both.

panels.description: Tight horizontal strip across Varma's eyes as they leave the map and settle on Nagoji. Dark. Steady. Nothing soft, nothing careless. Only Varma's eyes and brow in frame, face from the sheet only; if any headwear shows at the top edge it is the cream-and-gold turban. No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kind of eyes that measure before they strike.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen them in generals' tents, and in men who held small forts against impossible odds.

panels.description: Two-shot from behind Nagoji's shoulder (bare-headed, curly hair tied back, cream shirt), the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma on the platform speaks, looking only at Nagoji (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder, gold necklaces). Ramayyan at the king's left hand (screen right), thin, in plain white cloth, no jewellery, translates a heartbeat later without taking his eyes off Nagoji either.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Maharaja asks if you were on the ship that broke near our fishermen's village.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes. I was.

panels.description: Wide and flat, the rhythm panel: a side view across the hall, with the open sea side behind the camera and the closed wall behind the figures. Left to right: Marthanda Varma on his raised platform (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth), Ramayyan at his low table at the platform's front corner (thin, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), and Nagoji standing on the floor below (village shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands, bare-headed, no chains, no weapon). Stagger the balloons left to right in the order Ramayyan, Nagoji, Ramayyan, Nagoji so the questions come fast.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He asks if you rode for the Peshwa.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You raided Portuguese outposts on the western roads that feed their ports.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did.

panels.description: Varma's hand in the foreground, two fingers extended toward Nagoji's bandaged fingers: only his hand, a gold bangle and the edge of his cream-and-gold cloth are in frame, his head out of frame. Nagoji's wrapped hands at the far edge of frame, still at his sides against his cream shirt.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: They questioned you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They tried.

panels.description: Small. Varma, close, facing the camera, the open side of the hall behind him on screen left (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; gold necklaces). Something like amusement at the corners of his eyes, already fading. His eyes have moved on before any translation could have reached him. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If he understood my answers without his minister's help, he gave no sign beyond the speed of his eyes.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Ramayyan in the near foreground at screen left (thin, plain white cloth, no jewellery), pointing with his stylus to a mat laid a few paces from the platform. Nagoji, bare-headed in his cream shirt, lowering himself onto it, stiff, favouring healing wounds.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Sit. Speak. Tell him how they fight now on your coast.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: How their forts stand, how their captains think, how quickly they bring ships when a local chief resists.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji seated on the mat, talking, one bandaged hand shaping a low wall in the air. Bleeding in behind him like a stain rather than a clean flashback border (the Chapter 1, panel 6.5 device): a Portuguese bastion at Chaul, thick and low, a cannonball skipping off its slope in a spray of stone dust.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the next while, time lost its edges.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: At Chaul and Daman they build bastions thick and low, so cannonballs skip off instead of biting deep.

panels.description: Large, the page's biggest panel. The stain shifts and softens, because this is hearsay, not memory. It holds only two things: an anonymous padre, a stranger we have never met, in a plain black cassock with no white collar tab, walking ahead with a cross held high; and behind him a column of Portuguese musketeers in broad tilted hats and buff leather coats with matchlocks, not red, not blue. Nagoji small at the lower edge, seated on his mat, still talking. At the foreground edge, Varma's hand makes one small tap on the spear shaft; only the hand and the shaft are in frame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Our clerks said their padres walk ahead of the soldiers talking of one God, while the men behind count how many guns a king can spare.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We heard of rajas who signed, thinking European friends would keep neighbours away. They had invited a hungry wolf into their courtyards.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Varma leaning forward over the unrolled map (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, gold necklaces), one finger on a point where a river mouth meets the sea. Inset, top left corner of the panel: Ramayyan's hand and stylus, still until now, scratching fast on a palm leaf.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off, in the inset)
copy.text: And their infantry do not know what to do with sudden horse on the flank.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Here. This river mouth. How many days from their nearest stronghold at full sail?

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed, eyes closed. Behind him, the stain: the coastline seen from a galloping horse's back, sails far out on the water, a Portuguese warehouse burning on a quay at night.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of wind, and of how many days their replacement ships had taken to arrive.

panels.description: Nagoji opening his eyes, answering the king directly. Reverse angle, the open side on screen right.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the wind favours them, three days. Four if they are unlucky.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Longer if someone whispers wrong directions into the ear of a pilot.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma's head lifted from the map, eyes narrowed, mouth open on a sharp word (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, thin, in plain white cloth, lips still closed, stylus paused mid-stroke: the king has reacted before the translation.

copy.speaker: VARMA (sharp)
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

panels.description: Nagoji, level, speaking to the king and not to the diwan. Reverse angle, the open side on screen right.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: You mistrust pilots?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I mistrust everyone who touches a coin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But men who steer ships can be made to see profit in many directions.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. The corner of Varma's mouth twitches; he does not turn his head (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in plain white cloth, is already writing, and does not look up either.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ram.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (soft)
copy.text: Already marked, Maharaja.

panels.description: Wide, from the entrance end, the open side of the hall on screen left. The hall gone still, as if waiting for something. Marthanda Varma on his platform speaks at length, even-toned, the spear upright beside him (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). Ramayyan in white cloth at his left hand. Nagoji seated on his mat before the platform, his back to us. The seated rows motionless. Through the open side, the sea.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I caught none of the words. Only the weight.

panels.description: Low angle from floor level just before the platform, looking up past its edge, the open side of the hall on screen left. Ramayyan at near right (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), translating, his stylus held still above the leaf. Behind him and to the left, Marthanda Varma sits motionless with his spear upright (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says you speak as if you have counted men and ships for years.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yet your own masters failed to keep you from their dungeons.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed in his cream shirt. Jaw set; he does not drop his eyes. His bandaged hands have closed on his knees, gripping the cloth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not meant as an insult. It was simple fact. Still, it stung.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Any war has its losses. I misjudged a patrol near the coast. I paid the price.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That does not make my other calculations less true.

panels.description: Wide from behind Nagoji's mat, the open side of the hall on screen left. On the platform Marthanda Varma, unreadable, speaks briefly (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in white cloth, turns his head across the hall toward Ibrahim, who stands at the open-side edge of the clear space (screen left) with his hands folded over his pockets (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says, perhaps.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: And he asks Ibrahim if he trusts you.

panels.description: Medium, seen from the platform side, the open side of the hall on screen right. Ibrahim at the open-side edge of the clear space, easy, spreading his hands: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets over a pale vest and white mundu. He faces the platform, so the open side is at his left, and the sea light from it catches the scar along his LEFT jaw. Pillars and bright sea behind him.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: As far as one can trust a man who owes you his life and hates the same enemies.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Beyond that, trust is for priests.

panels.description: Small panel, one moment only. Varma with his head tipped back a fraction in a single short laugh (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A dry sound that needed no translation.

panels.description: The page's largest panel, wide, from the hall, the open side on screen left. Varma, after a long silent look at the man on the mat, sweeps one hand toward the open side, where the inlet, the moored boats and the red stone outer wall show below (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth, gold necklaces). Ramayyan at his left hand (screen right), thin, in plain white cloth, translating.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says they already have horse from the Nayak of Madurai, and Nair warriors who fight on foot or on small horses in this soil.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They have Dutch fortifications in their minds, thanks to other Europeans who chose to be practical rather than loyal.

panels.description: Close on Varma, face unreadable, eyes on the guest below him; the question is his (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; gold necklaces). The open side of the hall behind him on screen left. The diwan is off panel. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: He asks what you add that he does not already have.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the same question they had asked in the compound. But this man could, with a word, send me back to the Portuguese.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Point-of-view shot from a seated position on the mat before the platform, looking sideways out between the pillars of the open side of the hall, no figures in the foreground: the inlet below, the moored boats, men small as ants along the shore unloading sacks and checking nets. Beyond them the sea, flat and deceptive, to a hard, empty horizon. Keep the sky open for two captions.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere beyond that horizon sat Goa, with its dungeons.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere farther still, Dutch hulls cut through foaming water, carrying men who believed pepper and souls could belong to them by right.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed, bandaged hands on his knees, his eyes coming back from the open side to the king. Slow. He is not pleading; he is laying out terms.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have horse from Madurai. You have Nair warriors who know this land as they know their own pulse.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have guns and forts and men from across the sea who teach you how Europeans think.

panels.description: Large, full width, the page's biggest panel, about 40 percent of the page. The stain again, the largest yet, in warm stained tones: Kanka, the black mare of Chapter 1, on wet sand near Chaul, and low over her neck the memory rider, Nagoji BEFORE his capture, in Maratha cavalry dress (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, talwar), hands unbandaged. Other Maratha riders in turbans and cream tunics come in beside him. A line of Portuguese musketeers (broad tilted hats, buff leather coats, matchlocks; not British red, not Dutch blue) flinching and falling out of order as the horses come in at an angle they never drilled for. No blood. At the bottom edge, in normal colour, the present-day Nagoji small, seated on his mat: bare-headed, cream shirt, bandaged hands, speaking.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What you do not yet have is someone who has ridden into a European line and felt it break.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Someone who has watched their neat formations falter not from fear of God, but because a hoof struck at the right moment in the right place.

panels.description: Narrow, cold. The stain turns: only Keshavrao's eyes, huge in storm light, rain across them, at the hatch of the breaking ship. He is about nineteen, beardless, with no scar, black hair hacked short and plastered wet. No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Keshavrao.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And the weight I now carried.

panels.description: Medium side view across the hall, as in 4.1, with the open sea side behind the camera. Nagoji on his mat at screen right, leaning in toward the platform edge at screen left, voice lower and harder: bare-headed, cream shirt, bandaged hands. Dark rafters and open hall space above him for the balloons.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I can help you turn speed into a weapon against men who think their guns make them untouchable.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I can show your riders where to strike, when to pull away, how to make men who drilled on flat European fields die confused on this coast.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the hall, the open side on screen left: the hall silent, a bird on the parapet outside, waves on the sand below. Varma on his platform taps the butt of his spear against the mat, once, twice (two small motion ticks), eyes never leaving the man on the mat (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ram.

panels.description: Medium on Ramayyan at his low table (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), having inclined his head to the king, now turned to the man on the mat below and speaking to him directly, in Konkani, before any word from the king. The king is out of frame. Sea light from screen left.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Madurai horsemen know the straight charge. They do not know the feint and vanish the way Deccan riders do.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Our Maravar riders fight bravely, but not yet with discipline against guns.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You could help shape that.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma with a thin smile for his minister, his gaze already back on the mat below as he speaks briefly (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in white cloth, amused. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says I always see the two faces of the coin. And he says, very well, Nagoji Sawant.

panels.description: Tight on Ramayyan, still faintly amused, eyes sharp on the man below, delivering it lightly (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: For now, you are not a guest. You are not yet a servant either.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are an experiment.

panels.description: Full width. Varma in profile in the near left third, facing screen right, glancing out toward the open side of the hall (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). The view between the pillars fills the right two thirds: below the fort, a narrow strip of wet sand pinned between a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms and the sea. This is the ground of Chapter 7; plant it clearly. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Outside this fort a strip of shore runs along the sea, too wet for most cavalry, too narrow for big batteries. It is where the Dutch will expect us to be weakest.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the entrance end, high, the open side of the hall on screen left. Nagoji small on his mat before the platform, bare-headed in his cream shirt; Marthanda Varma (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest) and Ramayyan (plain white cloth, at the king's left hand) on the platform above him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders, and show him something there he has not already imagined.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If you are wrong, you will find Travancore worse than the Portuguese.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his feet before the platform, straightening despite the pull of healing wounds: bare-headed, cream shirt, dhoti, bandaged hands, unarmed.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: As he commands.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma, voice lower, looking only at the man below (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand Ramayyan, in white cloth, translating quietly. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says I am to give you what you need. And you are not to waste men.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat. He does not throw them away lightly, not even when the gods demand it.

panels.description: Outside. Ramayyan (thin, plain white cloth, no jewellery), palm leaves under one arm, leads Nagoji out between the carved pillars onto the top of the stone steps. Nagoji is bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt. Wind off the sea in his hair, the surf loud below.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Come. Let us see what a storm can do when given horse instead of chains.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Storms had tried to kill me. Now I would learn whether I could become one.

panels.description: Medium close on Nagoji's hip and hand: his bandaged hand has gone to his hip and rests on the plain knot of his cotton dhoti, below the hem of his cream shirt. The hip is bare of any weapon: NO sword, NO scabbard, NO sash, NO belt. The stone step and the bright sea beyond are out of focus.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (italic)
copy.text: *I will serve this king. I will harden his riders and break his enemies.*

copy.speaker: CAPTION (italic)
copy.text: *When that debt is paid, I will turn north again, find Chimaji, and burn the Portuguese out of Goa, stone by bloody stone.*

Nagoji from behind at the top of the steps, bare-headed, cream shirt and dhoti, his bandaged hand still resting at his hip on the dhoti knot: NO sword, NO scabbard, NO sash.
